title: Fleet growth pushes total connections past the database's server-side limit
source_note: Failure pattern (cumulative connection demand from a growing fleet with fixed per-instance pools crossing the database's max_connections, so new connections are refused server-side) is a standard capacity class in the Google SRE Book. All services, numbers, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~11:30 UTC orders-service is intermittently failing with database connection errors - about 15% of requests. No deploys. The fleet was scaled up this morning for load.

signal_lines.msg: connection count 495/500 (max_connections); new connections being refused
FATAL: sorry, too many clients already; ~15% of requests failing to acquire a DB connection
connection slots exhausted; superuser_reserved_connections in use
total pool demand = 52 instances x 10 connections = 520, exceeds max_connections 500
operator lowered per-instance pool to 8 and raised max_connections to 600; refusals stopped

ground_truth.root_cause: The database's server-side connection limit (max_connections = 500) was reached. Each orders-service instance holds a static pool of 10 connections; the fleet had grown over the week and an autoscale from 40 to 52 instances that morning brought total pool demand to 52 x 10 = 520, exceeding 500. The database began refusing new connections ('too many clients already'), so ~15% of requests failed to acquire a connection. There was no code deploy - the cause is cumulative connection demand crossing the fixed limit, tipped over by the morning's scale-up. Recovery required lowering the per-instance pool size and raising max_connections.
evidence_path: autoscaler INFO: orders-service scaled 40 -> 52 instances that morning
orders-db WARN: connection count 495/500 (max_connections), refusing new connections
orders-service ERROR: 'too many clients already'; ~15% of requests fail to acquire a DB connection
orders-db notes total pool demand 52 x 10 = 520 exceeds max_connections 500
refusals stop after the per-instance pool is lowered to 8 and max_connections raised to 600
ground_truth.fix: Lower the per-instance pool and raise max_connections (done). Put a connection pooler (e.g. PgBouncer) between the fleet and the database so server-side connections do not scale linearly with instance count, and alert when connection count approaches the limit.
